text: This FiftyFive Technologies Policy on separation policy is released for use in FiftyFive Technologies Pvt Limited with effect from 01 January 2026. This document is subject to FiftyFive Technologies Pvt Limited Procedure and subject to change any time as per the company policy.
Employee Initiated Separation (Resignation)
Company Initiated Separation
Abandonment of Employment by Employee
Retirement To review the detailed policy for each type of employee separation, please refer to the explanations provided below.

Employee Initiated Separation (Resignation) Policy Overview Employee Initiated Separation refers to a voluntary resignation initiated by the employee. For all purposes, the date of intimation of resignation shall be considered as the start date for computing the notice period. Wherein the Employee desires to part ways with the organization & initiates separation. With reference to the clause of “Letter of Employment”. For all purposes, the date of intimation of resignation will be the start date for computing the notice period duration. Process to apply
Employees must submit their resignation through the HRMS portal (KEKA), addressed to their Project Manager and Head of HR.
Upon acceptance of resignation, employees are required to serve the notice period as per Company policy, subject to completion of No Dues Clearance.
Before relieving, the employee must obtain a No Dues Certificate from all relevant departments, confirming that there are no pending dues, obligations, or issues with the Company.

Only after completion of the notice period and clearance of all obligations will the employee be formally relieved and eligible for final settlement. Confidentiality of Resignation Resignation is a sensitive matter and must be treated with strict confidentiality by the employee, the Reporting Manager, and the Company. Details of the resignation, including intent, notice period, and last working day, shall not be disclosed to other employees, clients, or external parties unless required for business continuity or formally communicated by the HR Department. Any breach of confidentiality may attract disciplinary action as per Company policy. Notice Period Requirements:
Duration of Notice Period: In case you desire to leave the services of the company following terms and conditions will be applied:
In the case of full-time employees, employees shall have to serve at least 3 months’ notice.
In the case of a full-time employee on a probation or intern on an Intern Trainee Period, the employee shall have to serve a notice of 2 months.
The notice period for all employees, as specified in this policy or the Offer / Appointment Letter, is mandatory and non-negotiable.

The release shall be considered solely at the discretion of the Company, on a case-by-case basis, and will be subject to business requirements and prior to written approval from both the Reporting Manager and the HR Department. Employees acknowledge that the Company’s decision regarding early release shall be final and binding. ii) Notice Period Waiver & Last Working Day:
Any request for a notice of period waiver or early release shall be considered strictly at the sole discretion of the Company and on a case-by-case basis, subject to business requirements.

A notice of period waiver, whether partial or full, shall be granted only upon prior written approval from both the Reporting Manager and the HR Department. Employees shall not assume or communicate an early release unless such approval is formally granted.

In the event a notice period waiver is approved, the Last Working Day (LWD) shall be mutually discussed, finalized, and frozen in writing between the employee, Reporting Manager, and HR. Once frozen, the LWD shall not be altered without further written approval from the Company.

The Company reserves the right to withdraw or revise an approved waiver if business exigencies, incomplete handover, policy non-compliance, or performance issues arise during the notice period. Grant of a notice period waiver does not absolve the employee from completing all exit formalities, work handover, asset return, and No Dues clearance as per Company policy. iii) Last Working Day (LWD) Determination:
The Last Working Day (LWD) shall be determined based on the date of resignation submission, the applicable notice period, and the formal acceptance of resignation by the Company.

The LWD shall be calculated from the date of resignation intimation, which shall be considered the start date for computing the notice period, unless otherwise specified in the employee’s Offer or Appointment Letter.

Any change to the originally calculated LWD, including early release or extension of the notice period, shall be made only with prior written approval from the Reporting Manager and the HR Department.
The LWD shall be formally communicated in writing to the employee by the HR Department and once communicated, shall be treated as final and frozen.

The Company reserves the right to revise or extend the LWD in cases including but not limited to incomplete work handover, pending deliverables, policy violations, excessive absenteeism, or business requirements.

Completion of all exit formalities, including work handover, asset return, and No Dues clearance, is mandatory up to the confirmed LWD. Failure to comply may result in delay of relieving, withholding of Full & Final Settlement, or other actions as per Company policy. Work Handover & Transition

During the notice period, the employee is required to ensure a complete, accurate, and timely handover of all assigned responsibilities, ongoing tasks, projects, client communications, data, documents, credentials (where applicable), and knowledge to the designated successor or team, as instructed by the Management.

The handover and transition must be completed to the full satisfaction of the Reporting Manager and the Management of the Company. This includes, but is not limited to, documentation, system access updates, training sessions, and knowledge transfer meetings.
The Company reserves the right to extend the notice period or revise the Last Working Day (LWD) if the handover is found to be incomplete, unsatisfactory, or disruptive to business continuity.

Failure to complete a proper handover, refusal to cooperate during the transition, or non- compliance with handover instructions shall be treated as a breach of Company policy and may result in disciplinary action, delay or denial of relieving, withholding or adjustment of Full & Final Settlement, and/or legal action, subject to applicable laws.

Completion of work handover is a mandatory condition for issuance of the Experience Letter, Relieving Letter, and processing of Full & Final Settlement. Asset Return & System Access Revocation All Company assets issued to the employee, including but not limited to laptops, desktops, mobile phones, ID cards, access cards, documents, files, software, licenses, data storage devices, and any other Company property, must be returned in good condition on or before the Last Working Day (LWD), as per the Company’s Asset Policy. The Company reserves the right to recover costs, withhold relieving documents, delay the Full & Final Settlement, or take appropriate action, in case of loss, damage, non-return, or misuse of Company assets, in accordance with the Asset Policy. System access including email, internal tools, applications, VPN, HRMS, and client systems shall be revoked as per the Company’s Asset Policy and exit process, during or upon completion of exit formalities. Confidentiality & Data Security Post-Separation All obligations relating to confidentiality, non-disclosure, data protection, intellectual property, and information security, as agreed under the Letter of Employment or any other agreement, shall continue to remain binding even after cessation of employment. The employee shall not, directly or indirectly, use, disclose, copy, retain, or share any confidential information, proprietary data, client information, trade secrets, or internal Company materials for post separation. Any breach of confidentiality or misuse of Company data post-exit may result in legal action and recovery of damages, subject to applicable laws. Misconduct During Notice Period Any act of misconduct, indiscipline, policy violation, performance negligence, or unethical behavior during the notice period shall be dealt with in accordance with Company disciplinary procedures. The Company reserves the right to terminate employment during the notice period in cases of serious misconduct, without prejudice to its rights under applicable laws, and such termination may impact eligibility for relieving documents and Full & Final Settlement. Bonus & Incentive Eligibility On the date of resignation, termination, or during the notice period, as applicable, the employee shall not be eligible for any bonuses, incentives, or variable pay, including but not limited to performance bonus, retention bonus, referral bonus, or any other form of monetary or non- monetary incentive or appreciation. Any bonus or incentive, if announced but not disbursed prior to the resignation date, shall stand forfeited, unless otherwise expressly approved in writing by the Company. Eligibility for any bonus or incentive shall be subject to the employee being on active rolls and not serving a notice period on the date of payout, as per Company policy. Resignation Month & Leave Rules
The month in which an employee submits their resignation shall be considered as the “Resignation Month.”

During the resignation month and the entire notice period, all categories of leave including earned leave, casual leave, additional leave, maternity leave, paternity leave, floater leave, compensatory offs, exam leave, and accrued leave balances or any other leave type shall remain on hold and shall not be availed.

Any leave taken during the resignation month or notice period shall be treated as Loss of Pay (LOP). Full and Final Settlement dues shall be processed only upon completion of the notice period and fulfillment of all exit formalities.

Excessive absenteeism, frequent leave, or any unauthorized or unapproved LOP during the notice period shall be treated as a breach of Company policy and may result in disciplinary action in accordance with Company procedures and/or extension of the notice period at the sole discretion of the Company.

In such cases, the Company reserves the right to withhold, adjust, or delay the Full and Final Settlement, subject to statutory compliance, until all obligations, handover requirements, and exit formalities are duly completed.

All leave or LOP requests during the notice period must be applied for in advance and shall be considered valid only upon written approval from both the Reporting Manager and the HR Department. Exit Formalities:
Exit Interview and Payroll Hold Guidelines
Exit interviews will be conducted as per process with the employee on his/her last working day.

If your resignation acceptance date, which is your last working date, has been decided and is falling before or on the date of 20th of the month perhaps your salary for the previous month and the current month would be on hold. For Example: If XYZ has its last working day on 15th of March, therefore his salary for the months of February and March would be on hold.

If your resignation acceptance date, which is your last working date, has been decided and falls after the date of the 20th of the month, perhaps your salary for only the current month would be on hold. For Example: If XYZ has its last working day on 25th of March, therefore his salary for the month of March would be on hold. ii) No Dues Clearance A No Dues Form must be completed and signed on behalf of the employee during the notice period and mandatorily on the last working day at FiftyFive Technologies Pvt. Limited. The form must be signed by all relevant departmental heads as specified. iii) Full & Final Settlement Upon formal acceptance of resignation, the employee’s salary for the notice period will be included in the full and final settlement, which shall be processed and cleared within 30–45 working days from the employee’s last working day. The settlement will be subject to deductions, recoveries, or adjustments as per Company policies, statutory requirements, and any applicable agreements. Components of Full & Final Settlement: The F&F may consist of:
Payment of Unpaid Salary (if any)
Notice Period Payment
Gratuity (as per eligibility criteria)
Provident Fund (as per eligibility)
Courier reimbursement (if any)
PL encashment (if any)

Relieving Letter iv) Gratuity Eligibility and Payment Policy This policy outlines the eligibility criteria, calculation, and payment process of gratuity to employees at the time of separation, including resignation, retirement, termination, superannuation, or death, in compliance with the Payment of Gratuity Act, 1972 and applicable provisions under the new Labour Laws / Labour Codes in India. Eligibility for Gratuity An employee shall be eligible for gratuity if they have completed five (5) or more years of continuous service with the Company. Exception: The requirement of five years of continuous service shall not apply in the event of:
Death of the employee
Permanent disablement of the employee In such cases, gratuity shall be payable to the nominee or legal heir, as applicable. Payment of Gratuity Gratuity shall become payable once:
The employee’s exit or separation process is completed, and

Eligibility is verified as per applicable law The payment shall be made in accordance with statutory timelines prescribed under the Payment of Gratuity Act. Forfeiture of Gratuity Gratuity may be partially or fully forfeited, strictly in accordance with the Payment of Gratuity Act, in cases where an employee’s services are terminated due to:
Fraud, theft, or dishonesty
Riotous or disorderly conduct

Acts involving moral turpitude committed during the course of employment Any forfeiture shall be applied only to the extent permitted under law. Governing Law This policy shall be governed by and interpreted in accordance with:
The Payment of Gratuity Act, 1972
Applicable provisions of the new Labour Codes
Rules, notifications, and amendments issued by the Government of India from time to time In the event of any inconsistency, statutory provisions shall prevail.
Privilege Leave and Encashment Policy

Privilege Leave (PL) encashment shall be calculated based on the employee’s last drawn basic salary at the time of separation. PL cannot be adjusted against the notice period and cannot be availed as leave during the notice period.
Encashment is allowed only after the completion of the year in which the PL was earned, subject to eligibility criteria.
Encashment of PL is processed at the time of exit or as per Company policy.
Privilege Leave can be encashed at the rate of basic pay applicable in the year the leave was earned.
PL encashment will be paid along with the final settlement of salary.
Payment will be calculated based on the basic salary and the number of PL days eligible for encashment.
Encashment is subject to deductions as per statutory or Company policies.
Any misuse or misrepresentation regarding PL, including unauthorized leave claims or encashment requests, may result in denial of PL encashment and other disciplinary actions.
This policy is subject to change at the discretion of the Company, in accordance with applicable laws and business requirements. vi) PF (Provident Fund) at the Time of Exit
Applicability Provident Fund benefits are applicable to all eligible employees covered under the Employees’ Provident Funds & Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952, and applicable rules thereunder.
Both the employee and employer contribute to the Provident Fund as per statutory rates
Contributions are deducted and deposited on a monthly basis during the period of employment
PF contributions continue until the employee’s last working day
PF at the Time of Separation
At the time of exit (resignation, termination, retirement, or superannuation):
The Company shall deposit PF contributions up to the employee’s last working month
The employee becomes eligible to:
Transfer PF balance to a new employer’s PF account, or
Withdraw PF balance, subject to eligibility conditions prescribed by law
PF Withdrawal / Transfer
PF withdrawal or transfer shall be initiated by the employee through the EPFO portal
Withdrawal is generally permitted:
After 2 months of unemployment, or
Immediately in case of retirement, superannuation, permanent disablement, or death
PF transfer is recommended if the employee joins another PF-covered organization
Employer Role The Company shall:
Update the employee’s date of exit with EPFO within statutory timelines
Provide necessary support and documentation required for PF withdrawal or transfer
The Company shall not be responsible for delays caused due to:
Incorrect details submitted by the employee
Non-completion of EPFO formalities by the employee
Taxation PF withdrawal may be subject to income tax as per applicable provisions, especially where:
Continuous service is less than five (5) years, or
PAN details are not updated with EPFO
Tax treatment shall be governed by the Income Tax Act and EPFO rules in force at the time of withdrawal.
Death of Employee In case of death:
PF balance shall be payable to the nominee or legal heir
The five-year service condition is not applicable
Necessary claims shall be processed as per EPFO rules
Governing Law This PF policy shall be governed by and interpreted in accordance with:
Employees’ Provident Funds & Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952
Rules, schemes, notifications, and amendments issued by the Government of India from time to time In case of any inconsistency, statutory provisions shall prevail. Legal Binding & Compliance

This policy shall be legally binding on the employee. Any violation, non-compliance, or breach of the terms stated herein may result in the Company taking appropriate disciplinary and/or legal action, as deemed necessary.

In the event of such action, the employee shall be held fully responsible for all costs, fees, expenses, and any losses or damages incurred by the Company arising out of or in connection with such violation, subject to applicable laws.

The Company reserves the right to enforce this policy in addition to any other rights or remedies available under the Letter of Employment, applicable agreements, and prevailing laws. Final Authority & Policy Interpretation In the event of any ambiguity, dispute, or difference in interpretation of this policy, the decision of the Company shall be final and binding, subject to applicable laws. The Company reserves the right to amend, modify, or withdraw this policy at any time without prior notice, in line with business requirements and statutory compliance.

Company Initiated Separation It is understood and agreed upon that: The company reserves the right to terminate the employment of an employee. The reasons here could be non-performance/On PIP or misconduct of the employee or non- adherence to the company policies by the employee such as manipulation of records, unethical behavior, integrity issues, etc. In such cases, the company can terminate the service immediately without giving any notice, whether in the probation period or being full-time which can be through email, in writing, or through the HRMS portal. OR in a situation, if a company decides to close its line of business or downsize the business, in such case the employer will give notice for one month or a month’s salary in lieu of notice period. In such a case the confirmation clause which states the notice period of 30 days for confirmed employees, stands void.

Misconduct or breach of any service Condition If you are found guilty of any misconduct, or commit any breach of the service conditions, or get involved in an act which in the opinion of the company is prejudicial to the interest of the company, the company may without any prior notice, terminate your services. The Company’s decision as to the occurrence of any event mentioned above shall be final. You shall not be entitled to the same question on any grounds whatsoever. ii) Termination as a result of non-performance All employees are expected to perform to a reasonable standard. In case the performance is unacceptable, the employee may be given a fair chance to improve. Written/verbal warnings maybe given as a matter of last resort to inform the employee of her/his performance. No improvement may result in the letter /email wherein the employee will be given a final chance to prove her/his performance. This letter will be treated as a “Notice of termination” if the performance is not satisfactory after one month from date of issue of such notice and the services of the employee can be terminated with immediate effect with no requirement of the notice period or pay in lieu thereof. iii) Termination for Serious Misconduct Your services may be terminated without notice for serious misconduct. Serious misconduct includes, but is not limited to:
Harassment of a work colleague or customer

Serious or repeated failure to follow a reasonable instruction; iv) Liability for Employee after Termination/Resignation/Retirement In the event of termination, resignation, or retirement, she/he will not represent the company either personally or by your agent directly as being in any way connected with your interest in the business of the company. You must abide by the following:
You will not disclose any of the Company’s customer details to anybody.
You will not contact or work with the Company’s customer without the Company’s permission.
You will keep the confidentiality of the source code/product developed or being developed in the company.
You will not use any of the source code developed by you in the Company.
You cannot put the customer's code or IO code on any of the public sites or websites or GitHub.
The company holds the rights to all the source code and products developed during your stay.

Abandonment of Employment by Employee An employee abandons himself or herself. This may be construed typically if an employee does not attend office for a continuous duration of over 3 working days without informing or seeking approval from the supervisor / Management or HR. In such a case the employee will be considered as absconding. The supervisor will inform HR and HR will follow up with the employee and wait for another 3 days. If the employee still does not report to the office after following ups, the employee will be declared absconding. In such a case, resignation acceptance, relieving letter will not be issued. The last working day will be taken as the last day reported to work. Recovery for the shortfall of notice period will be prepared.

Death of an Employee In the event of the death of the employee, the last date of office attended will be considered the last date of employment. Any amounts which are due to the Employee shall be payable to Employee’s heirs, successors or other legal representative which the employee has willfully nominated & are in the records of the company.

Retirement You will normally retire at the age of 58 years. In case the company desires to extend your services subsequent to you attaining the age of retirement, it will enter into a specific agreement with you and the sole authority for such extension will vest with the company. Standard Exit Guidelines: This policy shall be applicable to all forms of employee exit as mentioned under the above categories, including:
Employee-Initiated Separation (Resignation)
Company-Initiated Separation
Abandonment of Employment by an Employee
Retirement of an Employee Provisions:
Employees must apply resignation through KEKA mentioning the reason for leaving.
Employees should maintain the same standard of performance which was there before resignation.
In case smooth exit process not being followed, no relieving letter, Experience Letter and Full & Final settlement will be issued until all dues are settled.
Employees will abide by the policies and procedures of the company.
The Employee shall not disclose its resignation to the Clients of the Company unless prior written approval has been taken from the Reporting Manager / head of department.
All leaves will lapse; PL will be encashed in Full and Final Settlement.
Employees will not be eligible for any type of bonus during the Notice Period.

Any uninformed and unapproved leave during the notice period will lead to loss of pay. In case of utilization of excess leave balance, the notice period may be extended accordingly, subject to approval from the Reporting Manager and Head of HR. Full & Final Settlement: The full & final settlement is completed within 30- 45 days from the last working day of the employee after receiving ‘No Dues’ from all departments.
Calculation of Full & Final Settlement:

Salary on Hold: Held salary will be released in Full & Final Settlement after adjusting all financial Dues. ii) Leave Encashment: An employee’s accrued Privilege Leave (PL) balance is enchased in the F & F settlement. For the purpose of calculation, the current basic salary component of the employee is taken into account. All other types of unused leaves are automatically considered void.

Bonus & Incentives: Performance Bonus: Employee is eligible for Performance Bonus based on KRA achieved & its deliverables. The employee is to be engaged in billable project till his/her Last Working Day and in the rolls of the company when the Performance Bonus is being disbursed. The Reporting Managers scoring on KRAs achieved will be taken into account & amount prorated. Incentives: Incentives will be calculated on receivables only. Employees will be eligible for percentage calculation only on the amount received from the client till his/her last working day. Retention Bonus: An employee shall be eligible for the Retention Bonus based on the committed tenure as promised by the employee. In case the employee resigns prior to completion of the committed tenure, the Retention Bonus shall become null and void. Referral Bonus: The Referral Bonus shall be released only if the preferred candidate has successfully joined the organization and completed a probation period of three (3) months. In case the employee who made the referral resigns before completion of the referred employee’s probation period, the Referral Bonus shall become null and void.

Gratuity: This policy outlines the eligibility criteria, calculation, and payment process of gratuity to employees at the time of separation, including resignation, retirement, termination, superannuation, or death, in compliance with the Payment of Gratuity Act, 1972 and applicable provisions under the new Labour Laws / Labour Codes in India. Eligibility for Gratuity An employee shall be eligible for gratuity if they have completed five (5) or more years of continuous service with the Company. Exception: The requirement of five years of continuous service shall not apply in the event of:
Death of the employee
Permanent disablement of the employee In such cases, gratuity shall be payable to the nominee or legal heir, as applicable. Payment of Gratuity Gratuity shall become payable once:
The employee’s exit or separation process is completed, and

Eligibility is verified as per applicable law The payment shall be made in accordance with statutory timelines prescribed under the Payment of Gratuity Act. Forfeiture of Gratuity Gratuity may be partially or fully forfeited, strictly in accordance with the Payment of Gratuity Act, in cases where an employee’s services are terminated due to:
Fraud, theft, or dishonesty
Riotous or disorderly conduct

Acts involving moral turpitude committed during the course of employment Any forfeiture shall be applied only to the extent permitted under law. Governing Law This policy shall be governed by and interpreted in accordance with:
The Payment of Gratuity Act, 1972
Applicable provisions of the new Labour Codes
Rules, notifications, and amendments issued by the Government of India from time to time In the event of any inconsistency, statutory provisions shall prevail.

Privilege Leave (PL) Privilege Leave (PL) encashment shall be calculated based on the employee’s last drawn basic salary at the time of separation. PL cannot be adjusted against or availed during the notice period. Encashment is permitted only after completion of the year in which the PL was earned and is processed at the time of exit or as per Company policy. PL encashment will be paid along with the final settlement and is subject to statutory deductions. Employees are not eligible for PL encashment in cases of misconduct during the notice period, ongoing disciplinary issues, abandonment of employment, absconding, or any misuse of PL. The Company reserves the right to amend this policy in line with applicable laws and business requirements.
Deductions: The standard statutory deductions apply.
PF & any tax if applicable will be deducted in the Full & Final settlement.
Apart from this, any dues pending towards the company which includes not serving the notice period will be settled in the Full & Final statement.

Any company assets not returned or returned in unusable condition will be adjusted with an amount deemed fit by the management. Right to Amend Policies This Employee Handbook is intended to provide general guidance on Company policies and practices. FiftyFive Technologies reserves the right to amend, modify, suspend, or withdraw any policy, procedure, or benefit described in this handbook at any time, with or without notice, based on business, operational, or legal requirements.
